issues.location: VoltageToBit/Proofs/Contamination.lean lines 10-13 (module header; changed in fb8bc31)
issues.description: The header says: 'For the valid-input classes of the guarantee, which have no such range, there is no minimum delay', citing three lemmas. This says more than the library states, in two ways. (1) The header is about every record, but the three cited statements are about the illustrative record only. (2) The cited statements do not express 'no minimum delay'. valid_low_input_can_give_valid_high_within_38ps rules out only 38 ps. The two *_slew_unbounded lemmas say the right derivative at t = 0 can exceed any M, which is a statement about the instantaneous slope, not about how long the output takes to reach the valid level. For the fall direction no delay statement exists at all. No statement of the library says that for every δ > 0 a valid input can make the output valid within δ. The claim is plausibly true for the illustrative record (the 38 ps construction with a more negative input), but it is not stated. The wording comes from the fix that R3-05 itself suggested; adding the citations makes it read as proved. NegativeControls.lean says the precise thing: for these classes 'the three statements fail'.
issues.evidence: Read the cited statements (#check output in <scratch>/r5-comments/R5Claims.out): valid_low_rise_slew_unbounded : ∀ M, ∃ u v d, (∀ t, u t ≤ 0.40) ∧ v 0 = 0.25 ∧ IsTrajectory illustrative u v 0 10 ∧ HasDerivWithinAt v d (Ici 0) 0 ∧ M < d. The within_38ps statement fixes the instant 0.038. A scan of the HEAD type dump finds no statement with a delay quantified over δ.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: "For the valid-input classes of the guarantee, which have no such range, these lemmas give nothing, and the library states no minimum delay. For the illustrative record it shows that the range cannot be dropped: a valid-low input can give a valid-high output within 38 ps (`Examples.valid_low_input_can_give_valid_high_within_38ps`), and the rising slew over the valid-low class and the falling slew over the valid-high class have no bound (`Examples.valid_low_rise_slew_unbounded`, `Examples.valid_high_fall_slew_unbounded`)."

Verdict: not passed (2 blocking, 5 should-fix, 4 minor).

What holds. Every attack of the round-2 verdict now fails at the step that names it, for the right reason: an unpinned lakefile change stops at config; broken sources stop at build even with a repinned lakefile that has no default target or another one; the scoped instance in plain sight and behind `/-/-/`, the indented `variable?`, the oracle and native configurations and the hidden kernel bypass are refused by source-scan (and, where the compiled files show them, by axiom-audit); auto-bound names give [options] and [universes]; Bypäss.lean and Upper.LEAN give [tree]/[closure]; a hand-edited design record fails design-record. M7, M9 and M10 are fixed. The scan really reads what Lean reads, the audit sees scoped instances, the build is by name, and a full run deletes .lake/build and .lake/config. The records of the final full run (ffa58a1) regenerate byte for byte from a fresh copy in another directory (a path without spaces). --quick --fresh and --whole-env behave as documented. Nothing was written into R or its .lake/packages.

What fails is the identification of what was checked. (1) A module under VoltageToBit/__pycache__ is compiled and checked but never digested, and git ignores it, so the record does not pin it and --quick later calls a changed tree 'these same files'. (2) check.sh's own `python3 -c` programs import modules from the project directory, so a planted hashlib.py makes step 2's pin and the record's digests lie: a full run passed with a vacuous `chain_witness : 2 ≤ 1 → ∃ ...`, and four of its five records are byte for byte the committed ones. I rate (2) blocking because it is not covered by the hostile-library exclusion (no library code runs; check.sh executes the file) and the fix is one environment variable. The rubric's literal reading makes both blocking (a success line while a claim about the compiled files is false). Should-fix: a repinned lakefile can move the sources (srcDir) out from under the scan, the digests and step 6; the design-record check can be satisfied by a decoy; --quick trusts .lake/config; the record always says Mathlib was not recompiled; step 2 looks at HEAD only.

None of these constructs is in the committed tree: there is no __pycache__ under VoltageToBit/, no .py file in R's root, IllustrativeDesign.lean carries its header and matches, and lakefile.toml has no srcDir. My baseline run reproduced the committed records, so the committed evidence for the library itself is unaffected; the checks just would not have caught these cases. The tools' own temporary directories were under the system TMPDIR and were removed by their traps.
